_comment: Copy for the printed A4 handouts — one per trade, front is the pitch and back is the how. Written to be photocopied in black and white, read at arm's length by someone standing up, and pinned to a wall. Thai leads because the reader is Thai; English is there so a farang employer or a volunteer can follow the same sheet. Nothing here promises anything the site does not already do — a handout that oversells is a handout that gets shown to us later.
_shan_warning: The shn strings are an unverified machine attempt and MUST be checked by a Shan speaker before a single sheet is printed. make_handouts.py stamps every page with an UNVERIFIED banner until shanVerified is true below. Confidence is low: Shan is under-represented in the model that wrote these and the writer cannot read back what it produced. Separately, and this needs checking on the ground rather than taken from me: Shan literacy in Shan script is uneven among migrant workers in Chiang Mai, and many read Thai script more comfortably. If that holds, the Thai column is doing most of the work and the Shan column is doing something else — signalling that they were thought of, which is not nothing.
